set.approach: Park at the Zopkios rest area off Highway 5 and walk east along the highway shoulder to a cairned climbers' trail that climbs steeply through forest and talus to the foot of Yak's big south-facing slabs. The climb starts left of Yak Crack, whose opening pitches follow a large dihedral that is easy to pick out from the base.

review.notes: Approach from area page and Yak Crack/Yak Check location text; the route page only says it starts left of Yak Crack. Descent skipped: the page says the route stops short of the summit but not how to get off.

set.descent_text: The route ends at a tree anchor with many slings. From there you can scramble the remaining ledges, moss grooves and dirty cracks of sustained fourth class to the top, or rappel back down the route with two ropes. Once on top, the usual way off is the east-side walk-off: head for the saddle between the true summit and the false summit, where a snow patch often lingers into summer, then follow the trail down through the meadow bowl behind the peak. The trail drops steeply along the east flank and curls back around the foot of the south face to the approach trail. A stream often crosses the lower slabs there early in the season.
set.approach: Reach the base of the slabs by the west-side trail, which starts from the Zopkios rest area just east of the exit, or by the main climbers' trail. Then cross the base of the slabs toward the two small ponds below the route; if you reach a tarn beyond them you have gone too far, so backtrack. The route begins in the middle of the southwest face, by a stunted dead tree wearing a blue sling, under a faint pale streak.

review.notes: Route page for ending, scramble/rappel options, ponds and start; SOMWOW and Clyde and Isabelle pages confirm the west-side trail and ponds; Yak Check and SOMWOW for the east-side walk-off, hike page for saddle/meadow. No pitch counts or times given.

set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit. Parties can rappel the line, since every station is fixed, or take the standard walk-off. Once on top, the usual way off is the east-side walk-off: head for the saddle between the true summit and the false summit, where a snow patch often lingers into summer, then follow the trail down through the meadow bowl behind the peak. The trail drops steeply along the east flank and curls back around the foot of the south face to the approach trail. A stream often crosses the lower slabs there early in the season.
set.approach: Follow the main climbers' trail to the base of the wall, then turn right and follow the base to its high point, where a coffee-table-sized rock marks the start. The first bolt shows on the slab above, and easy slab and scrambling lead to it. The start is a good way right of Reality Check, close to where Madness begins. A snow patch lingers here late into June.

review.notes: Cardiyak page for summit finish, fixed stations and location; Wind Walker page for the shared start and snow patch; walk-off from Yak Check and SOMWOW. Rappel count omitted (single source).

set.descent_text: The route is fully bolted and finishes on the tree island that Speedway also reaches, but higher and further right. The usual way down is to rappel the line on the fixed stations with two ropes.
set.approach: Take the left-side trail, which leaves the highway a little east of the Zopkios rest area, up to the base of the slabs, and pass both small ponds. The route starts to the right of Speedway; its first bolt sits just above a prominent dish right of the Speedway start.

review.notes: Route page for finish, ropes and start; Coquihalla Honey page for double-rope rappels on fixed stations; Speedway and SOMWOW pages for the trail and ponds.

set.descent_text: The route stops at an arbitrary final belay beneath a large arching corner and does not top out. The bolted stations are fixed for rappelling, and two ropes are needed to get off.
set.approach: Take the left-side trail from the Zopkios rest area to the base of the slabs and pass the two small ponds, as for the neighbouring routes. The start is to the right of Clyde and Isabelle.

review.notes: Route page for ending, fixed rappels and location; Clyde and Isabelle, Speedway and SOMWOW for the trail and ponds.

set.descent_text: Walk off to the right, toward the meadow bowl, where you meet the normal descent trail. That trail runs down the east flank of the peak and curls around the foot of the south face to the approach trail.
set.approach: Hike the climbers' trail to the base of Yak Crack, then head right and follow the normal descent trail uphill through forest until it breaks out into the meadow bowl southeast of the peak. Cross the meadow to the left to reach the concave east face, which holds several curving dihedrals; the longest one is the central line.

review.notes: Route page for approach and walk-off direction; SOMWOW, Yak Check and hike page for the descent trail through the meadow bowl.

set.descent_text: The route joins the upper dihedral of Yak Crack, and once the climbing is done the best way down is to walk off. Once on top, the usual way off is the east-side walk-off: head for the saddle between the true summit and the false summit, where a snow patch often lingers into summer, then follow the trail down through the meadow bowl behind the peak. The trail drops steeply along the east flank and curls back around the foot of the south face to the approach trail. A stream often crosses the lower slabs there early in the season.
set.approach: From the base of the wall below the Yak Crack start, follow the foot of the slab up and to the right until the leftmost dihedral on the southeast face comes into view. It is the first dihedral left of the one Porcelain Chicken climbs. The dihedral can also be gained from the right, as for Porcelain Chicken.

review.notes: Route page for line, junction with Yak Crack and walk-off advice; Yak Crack for the walk-off; Yak Check/SOMWOW for the trail.

set.descent_text: The route eases into slab scrambling and ends at the summit. Once on top, the usual way off is the east-side walk-off: head for the saddle between the true summit and the false summit, where a snow patch often lingers into summer, then follow the trail down through the meadow bowl behind the peak. The trail drops steeply along the east flank and curls back around the foot of the south face to the approach trail. A stream often crosses the lower slabs there early in the season.
set.approach: From the base of the wall, start right of Reality Check and solo the long, easy-angled slabs, using a ramp through the overhang band to work up and right to the ledge below Porcelain Chicken. Madness climbs the rightmost dihedral on the southeast face, to the right of the Porcelain Chicken dihedral.

review.notes: Route page for approach and summit finish; Porcelain Chicken page for neighbouring dihedral; walk-off from SOMWOW/Yak Check/hike page. The row lists one pitch but the page describes several; no counts used.

set.approach: Take the climbers' trail from the highway and scramble a fair way up the descent trail, then cut hard left along a ledge to the base of the central dihedral on the southeast face. It is the most prominent dihedral on that face, between Hole in My Heaven and Madness.

review.notes: Approach from Porcelain Chicken page, with Hole in My Heaven and Madness pages placing it. Descent skipped: the route ends on a ledge well below the top and no source says how to get off from there.

set.descent_text: The final pitch is a fourth-class slab to trees, and from there you can scramble easily upward or rappel. Walking off is faster and safer than rappelling. From the trees, continue through an opening to the shoulder of the false summit, pass the false summit on its right by a short fourth-class ledge, and pick up the main trail. A steep snow patch can sit at the top of the descent; if you would rather avoid it, bolted rappel anchors on a small wall below the trail drop into the meadow. Follow the trail down through the meadow bowl and along the east flank, back to the foot of the south face.
set.approach: Take the climbers' trail from the highway up to the base of the south face. Start by scrambling easy slabs right of the start of Yak Crack.

review.notes: Route page for finish and walk-off advice; Yak Check for false-summit bypass, bolted rappels, trail. Times and rappel counts left out.

set.descent_text: From the top of pitch 14 you choose: rappel the route with two ropes from the chained stations if you are not going to the summit, or commit to the summit by scrambling a few hundred metres of fourth and fifth class through the meadow and ledges. Once on top, the usual way off is the east-side walk-off: head for the saddle between the true summit and the false summit, where a snow patch often lingers into summer, then follow the trail down through the meadow bowl behind the peak. The trail drops steeply along the east flank and curls back around the foot of the south face to the approach trail. A stream often crosses the lower slabs there early in the season.
set.approach: From the Zopkios rest area walk a short way east, and at the wrong-way sign look left into the trees for the west-side trail. It climbs to the base of the slab. Head east to the two small ponds below Speedway; the route starts just past the first pond, belayed from the dish next to it.

review.notes: SOMWOW page for approach, rappel and summit options, descent; Speedway, Clyde and Isabelle, Yak Check and hike page confirm the ponds, trail and east-side descent. Distances omitted.

set.approach: The approach is the same as for Speedway: reach the base of the slabs and cross toward the middle of the southwest face. The route follows the long gully on the left edge of the slabby south face; go up the floor of it and bear right where it forks.

review.notes: Route page says approach as per Speedway; Speedway and SOMWOW for that approach. Descent skipped: no source says where the route finishes.

set.descent_text: The route finishes at the summit. To walk off, scramble exposed fourth class up and right past shrubs, then back left to a flat spot in the trees where you can change into approach shoes. From there work up toward the summit block to a narrow, exposed ledge on the northeast side that leads to the hiking trail. Alternatively, rappel the route with two ropes; all anchors are fixed rings.
set.approach: Hike the Yak Peak trail up to the wall, then go right along its foot to the high point, where a rock the size of a coffee table marks the start. This is the same start as Cardiyak Rhythm, and easy slab and scrambling lead to the first bolt. Snow lingers at the base into June, and water often runs down the far right slab in July.

review.notes: Route page for descent options and start; Cardiyak page for shared start; Yak Check for the hiking trail on the east side.

set.descent_text: From the last belay, pass through a gap in the trees onto a level patch beside the false summit, where you can take off your harness. Climb toward the false summit and pass it on the right by a short fourth-class ledge to reach the main trail. The trail curves right into the meadow; a snow patch often remains into late summer, and two bolted anchors below the trail give a rappel into the meadow if the snow is too steep. From the meadow the trail drops steeply and curls back under the south face and onto the ramp you started up, which suits a pack left at the bottom. A stream often runs across the lower slabs.
set.approach: Park at the Zopkios rest area and follow the climbers' trail to the wall; after a talus field, cross to its left side to find the best trail. The route starts almost where the trail meets the wall, at a left-trending ramp. Scramble diagonally left up the ramp, third class, past a few bushes to a slabby groove, and gear up there.

review.notes: Yak Check page for descent and start; Reality Check page for the shared walk-off; Yak Crack and SOMWOW for east-side trail. Loose rock and a 2022 rockfall noted on the page are not stated as current.

set.descent_text: Finish up easy slabs to reach the walk-off. Once on top, the usual way off is the east-side walk-off: head for the saddle between the true summit and the false summit, where a snow patch often lingers into summer, then follow the trail down through the meadow bowl behind the peak. The trail drops steeply along the east flank and curls back around the foot of the south face to the approach trail. A stream often crosses the lower slabs there early in the season.
set.approach: Follow the climbers' trail from the highway up to the base of the wall, then look up and slightly left for the massive starting dihedral. Do not walk straight at it from below. Scramble slabs and ramps off to the right onto a ledge, then work back left across it to the dihedral's foot, where a bolted belay waits.

review.notes: Yak Crack page for approach and finish; walk-off from Yak Check/SOMWOW/hike page. Route text notes it can be combined with Reality Check pitches.
